title: All'ufficio anagrafe
subtitle: At the registry office
intro: A numbered ticket, a form in triplicate, a stamp that costs sixteen euros and is sold somewhere else. The comune is where you learn to say what you have already done, in the formal register, with patience. This unit closes A1: it adds the first past tense, the formal Lei in practice, ordinals and dates, and ends with the A1 checkpoint.
objectives: Say what you have done with the [[passato prossimo]]: [[ho compilato]], [[ho portato]], [[ho fatto]]
Use [[già]] and [[non… ancora]]: [[ho già pagato]], [[non ho ancora la marca]]
Give personal details formally and fill in a form: [[luogo e data di nascita]], [[stato civile]]
Use the ordinals and say how long: [[il primo]], [[il terzo piano]], [[da due mesi]]
Handle an office with [[Lei]]: [[Mi dica]], [[Scusi]], [[Si accomodi]], [[Firmi qui]]
canDo: A1 · Spoken interaction: can give personal details in a formal situation and understand simple questions about them.
A1 · Writing: can fill in a form with personal details (name, address, date and place of birth, nationality, marital status).
A1 · Spoken production: can say what they have done, in simple sentences, with time references.
A1 · Listening: can understand simple instructions in an office and the time and date of an appointment.
A1 · Reading: can understand a simple official notice, a form and an appointment slip.

sections.title: Numero dodici
sections.intro: Tuesday at the comune, Thursday again with the stamp. Listen for the passato prossimo (ho compilato, ho portato, ha pagato) and for the Lei forms (ha, mi dica, firmi, torni).

blocks.title: Mi dica
blocks.setting: Comune di Roccamarina, ufficio anagrafe, martedì ore 9. Il numero 12 in mano. Allo sportello, la dottoressa Antonella Moro, tre timbri e una pianta.

lines.t: Dodici! Buongiorno. Mi dica.
lines.n: Twelve! Good morning. How can I help?
lines.note: Mi dica: literally "tell me", the formal imperative. The standard opening at any counter.

lines.t: Buongiorno, dottoressa. Vorrei fare l'iscrizione anagrafica. La residenza.
lines.n: Good morning, dottoressa. I'd like to register as a resident. Residency.

lines.t: Ha compilato il modulo?
lines.n: Have you filled in the form?
lines.note: Ha compilato: the passato prossimo with Lei. Avere + participle in -ato.

lines.t: Sì, ho compilato il modulo e ho portato i documenti: passaporto, codice fiscale, contratto d'affitto.
lines.n: Yes, I've filled in the form and I've brought the documents: passport, tax code, rental contract.

lines.t: Ha già il codice fiscale?
lines.n: Do you already have the tax code?

lines.t: Sì. L'ho fatto la settimana scorsa all'Agenzia delle Entrate, a Lecce.
lines.n: Yes. I did it last week at the tax office, in Lecce.
lines.note: L'ho fatto: "I did it", with the pronoun lo (unit 10) and the irregular participle fatto.

lines.t: Bene. Luogo e data di nascita?
lines.n: Good. Place and date of birth?

lines.t: Toronto, il dodici marzo millenovecentonovantasei.
lines.n: Toronto, 12 March 1996.

lines.t: Stato civile?
lines.n: Marital status?

t.note: Unmarried: celibe for a man, nubile for a woman. On every Italian form. Single is also understood.

lines.n: Single.

lines.t: Cittadinanza italiana?
lines.n: Italian citizenship?

lines.t: Sì. Ho preso la cittadinanza due anni fa, a Toronto. Mio nonno è nato qui.
lines.n: Yes. I got my citizenship two years ago, in Toronto. My grandfather was born here.
lines.note: Ho preso: irregular participle of prendere. Due anni fa: two years ago. È nato: the passato prossimo with essere, unit 9.

lines.t: Manca la marca da bollo. Sedici euro. Dal tabaccaio, di fronte.
lines.n: The revenue stamp is missing. Sixteen euros. At the tobacconist's, opposite.

lines.t: Ma ho già pagato…
lines.n: But I've already paid…
lines.note: Già between avere and the participle.

lines.t: Ha pagato i diritti di segreteria. La marca da bollo è un'altra cosa. Non ha ancora la marca? Allora torni giovedì, con appuntamento. Alle dieci e un quarto. Firmi qui.
lines.n: You paid the administrative fee. The stamp is another thing. You don't have the stamp yet? Then come back on Thursday, by appointment. At a quarter past ten. Sign here.
lines.note: Torni, firmi: formal imperatives. Non… ancora: not yet.

notes.note: Registration in the town's population register: it makes you officially resident. Living there.
The question and the answer in the passato prossimo: Lei form ha, io form ho, same participle.

notes.phrase: due anni fa · la settimana scorsa
notes.note: Two years ago, last week. Fa after the time; scorso / scorsa after the noun.
… is missing. Mancare: to be missing, to be lacking. Manca la marca, mancano due fotocopie.

blocks.title: Giovedì, dieci e un quarto
blocks.setting: Martedì, la tabaccheria di fronte al comune. Poi giovedì, lo stesso sportello.

lines.t: Buongiorno. Una marca da bollo da sedici euro, per favore.
lines.n: Good morning. A sixteen-euro revenue stamp, please.

lines.t: Per il comune? Ecco. Sedici euro. Ha spiccioli?
lines.n: For the comune? Here. Sixteen euros. Do you have change?

lines.stage: Thursday, 10:15. No ticket this time: an appointment.

lines.t: Buongiorno. Ha portato tutto?
lines.n: Good morning. Have you brought everything?

lines.t: Ho portato tutto. Ho comprato la marca, ho fatto le fotocopie, ho scritto l'indirizzo sul modulo. Ho anche letto le istruzioni.
lines.n: I've brought everything. I bought the stamp, I made the photocopies, I wrote the address on the form. I even read the instructions.
lines.note: Fatto, scritto, letto: three irregular participles in one breath.

lines.t: Le istruzioni? Nessuno legge le istruzioni. Da quanto tempo è a Roccamarina?
lines.n: The instructions? Nobody reads the instructions. How long have you been in Roccamarina?
lines.note: Da quanto tempo è…? Present tense + da for "how long have you been".

lines.t: Da due mesi. Dal primo giugno.
lines.n: For two months. Since the first of June.
lines.note: Da due mesi: for two months. Dal primo giugno: since 1 June. Same da.

lines.t: Bene. Un vigile passa a casa per controllare. È normale. Poi arriva la lettera.
lines.n: Good. A municipal officer comes to the house to check. It's normal. Then the letter arrives.

lines.stage: Three stamps. A signature. A fourth stamp.

lines.n: Done. Welcome to Roccamarina, officially.

lines.t: Grazie, dottoressa. È stato… veloce.
lines.n: Thank you, dottoressa. That was… quick.
lines.note: È stato: it was. Essere's own passato prossimo, unit 9.

lines.t: Due visite. Per il comune è un record. Arrivederci.
lines.n: Two visits. For the comune it's a record. Goodbye.

notes.note: Do you have change (small coins)? Tobacconists and bars live on coins.
The municipal police officer (vigile urbano). For residency, one visits your address to confirm you live there. Be home, or leave a note.
Done. The participle alone, as a word. The most satisfying sound in Italian bureaucracy.

questions.q: The stamp is sold at the comune.
questions.why: At the tobacconist's opposite. Never at the office that requires it.

questions.q: How long has the protagonist been in Roccamarina?
questions.why: Da due mesi. Dal primo giugno.

questions.q: Ho ___ la marca, ho ___ le fotocopie, ho ___ l'indirizzo. (bought, made, wrote)
questions.n: I bought the stamp, made the photocopies, wrote the address.

sections.title: Documenti, moduli, uffici
sections.intro: The words on the form, the documents in the folder, the office and its rituals, and the verbs of getting things done, with their participles.

ex.t: Ha un documento? — Il passaporto.
ex.n: Do you have ID? — My passport.

items.note: Un documento = any official ID. I documenti = the papers.

ex.t: Ho due passaporti: canadese e italiano.
ex.n: I have two passports: Canadian and Italian.

ex.t: La carta d'identità si fa al comune.
ex.n: The ID card is issued at the comune.

items.note: Every Italian has one; residents can get one too. Now electronic (CIE).

ex.t: Senza codice fiscale non si fa niente.
ex.n: Without a tax code you can't do anything.

items.note: Sixteen letters and digits, from your name, birth date and place. Needed for contracts, phones, health card, everything.

ex.t: Con la residenza ho diritto alla tessera sanitaria.
ex.n: With residency I'm entitled to the health card.

items.note: Also carries the codice fiscale. Unit 12.

ex.t: Vorrei fare la residenza a Roccamarina.
ex.n: I'd like to register as resident in Roccamarina.

items.note: Prendere / fare / chiedere la residenza. L'iscrizione anagrafica is the official name.

ex.t: Un certificato di nascita, un certificato di residenza.
ex.n: A birth certificate, a residency certificate.

ex.t: Ho la cittadinanza italiana da due anni.
ex.n: I've had Italian citizenship for two years.

items.note: Cittadino / cittadina: citizen.

ex.t: Il contratto d'affitto è registrato.
ex.n: The rental contract is registered.

ex.t: Manca la marca da bollo da sedici euro.
ex.n: The sixteen-euro revenue stamp is missing.

items.note: A sticker you buy at the tabaccheria and stick on official papers. Sixteen euros is the standard one. Nobody knows why.

ex.t: Due fotocopie del passaporto, fronte e retro.
ex.n: Two photocopies of the passport, front and back.

items.note: Fare una fotocopia. Offices want copies; bring more than they ask.

ex.t: Ha compilato il modulo?
ex.n: Have you filled in the form?

items.note: Compilare un modulo: to fill in a form. In stampatello: in block capitals.

ex.t: Firmi qui. Manca la firma.
ex.n: Sign here. The signature is missing.

items.note: Firmare: to sign.

ex.t: Luogo di nascita: Toronto (Canada).
ex.n: Place of birth: Toronto (Canada).

items.note: Nascita: birth. Nato / nata a: born in. Nascere, unit 9.

ex.t: Data di nascita: 12/03/1996.
ex.n: Date of birth: 12/03/1996.

items.note: Day / month / year, like Canada's official format and unlike the US.

ex.t: Stato civile: celibe / nubile / coniugato / divorziato / vedovo.
ex.n: Marital status: single (m / f) / married / divorced / widowed.

items.note: Celibe (m.) and nubile (f.) for unmarried; coniugato/a or sposato/a for married; vedovo/a widowed.

ex.t: Indirizzo: via delle Rose 12, 73100 Roccamarina (LE).
ex.n: Address: Via delle Rose 12, 73100 Roccamarina (LE).

items.note: Street, number, postcode (CAP), town, province in brackets.

ex.t: Professione: meccanico di biciclette. Per ora: nessuna.
ex.n: Occupation: bicycle mechanic. For now: none.

ex.t: Il numero di telefono italiano comincia con 3.
ex.n: An Italian mobile number starts with 3.

items.note: Il cellulare, il telefonino: mobile phone. Also l'email, l'indirizzo email.

ex.t: Cognome e nome, in stampatello.
ex.n: Surname and first name, in block capitals.

items.note: Forms put the surname first. In stampatello: block letters.

ex.t: L'ufficio anagrafe è al primo piano.
ex.n: The registry office is on the first floor.

items.note: L'anagrafe: the population registry. L'ufficio postale, l'ufficio del turismo.

ex.t: Allo sportello tre, con il numero.
ex.n: At counter three, with the ticket number.

items.note: Lo sportello: s + consonant. Also the ATM slot and a car door.

ex.t: Ho un appuntamento giovedì alle dieci e un quarto.
ex.n: I have an appointment on Thursday at 10:15.

items.note: Prendere un appuntamento: to make one. Su appuntamento: by appointment only.

ex.t: L'impiegata è gentile ma precisa.
ex.n: The clerk is kind but precise.

ex.t: La pratica è chiusa. Fatto.
ex.n: The file is closed. Done.

items.note: Una pratica: one administrative matter from start to finish. Fare una pratica: to go through a procedure.

ex.t: Tre timbri e una firma.
ex.n: Three stamps and a signature.

items.note: Timbrare: to stamp. Not the marca da bollo, which is a sticker.

ex.t: Orario di apertura al pubblico: 8:30–13:00.
ex.n: Opening hours to the public: 8:30–13:00.

ex.t: L'ho fatto la settimana scorsa.
ex.n: I did it last week.

items.note: Scorso / scorsa after the noun: il mese scorso, l'anno scorso, lunedì scorso. Prossimo: next.

ex.t: Due anni fa. Un'ora fa. Poco fa.
ex.n: Two years ago. An hour ago. A short while ago.

items.note: After the time expression, like English.

ex.t: Ho compilato il modulo in stampatello.
ex.n: I filled in the form in block capitals.

items.note: Participle: compilato.

ex.t: Firmi qui. Ho firmato tre volte.
ex.n: Sign here. I signed three times.

ex.t: Ha portato tutto? — Ho portato tutto.
ex.n: Have you brought everything? — I've brought everything.

items.note: Also to carry and to wear (porto la M). Participle: portato.

sections.title: Ho fatto, ho già, da due mesi, Lei
sections.intro: Five pieces: the passato prossimo with avere, the irregular participles, ordinals and dates, da for "since" and "for", and the formal Lei in an office. Reference pages at the end of each block.

blocks.title: Passato prossimo with avere: ho compilato
blocks.rule: The past of most verbs: the present of avere + the past participle. Regular participles: -are → -ato, -ere → -uto, -ire → -ito. It covers English "I did", "I have done" and "I was doing something (once)". Già, ancora, mai, sempre go between avere and the participle.

blocks.caption: [[compilare]], [[ricevere]], [[finire]] · passato prossimo
blocks.note: The participle does not agree with the subject when the auxiliary is avere: ho compilato, whether Luca or Lucia is talking. With essere (unit 9) it does.

head: Italian
English
rows: I filled in / I've filled in the form.
Did you / have you filled in the form?
I didn't / haven't filled in the form.
Non ho mai visto il vigile.
ieri · la settimana scorsa · due anni fa · nel 2024 · stamattina · già · appena
yesterday · last week · two years ago · in 2024 · this morning · already · just

items.t: Ho portato i documenti e ho pagato i diritti.
items.n: I brought the documents and paid the fees.

items.t: Ieri Dora ha pulito le scale. Stamattina ha comprato il pane.
items.n: Yesterday Dora cleaned the stairs. This morning she bought bread.

items.t: Avete finito? — Non abbiamo ancora finito.
items.n: Have you finished? — We haven't finished yet.

items.t: Hai mai mangiato un pasticciotto? — Sì, ne ho mangiati tre.
items.n: Have you ever eaten a pasticciotto? — Yes, I've eaten three.
items.note: ne… mangiati: agreement with ne, unit 14; recognise
lo + ho → l'ho

blocks.title: One Italian tense, three English ones
blocks.text: [[Ho pagato]] = I paid, I have paid, I did pay. Italian does not separate "finished past" from "relevant to now" the way English does with the simple past and present perfect: the passato prossimo does both. The imperfetto (unit 11) covers "I was paying" and "I used to pay".

items.wrong: Io compilato il modulo. Ho compilare.
Ho già pagato → Già ho pagato. Ho pagato già.
Non ho pagato ancora. (acceptable in speech) / Non ancora ho pagato.
items.why: Ancora, like già, goes in the middle.

blocks.title: The first irregular participles
blocks.rule: Many -ere verbs and a few others have irregular participles. The nine most useful now: fatto, detto, preso, messo, visto, letto, scritto, aperto, chiuso. Learn each with its verb.

head: Verb
Participle
Example
rows: Ho fatto le fotocopie. Che cosa hai fatto ieri?
Ha detto: torni giovedì. Cosa ha detto?
Ho preso il numero. Ho preso la cittadinanza.
Ho messo la marca sul modulo.
Hanno aperto alle otto e mezza.
blocks.note: Families: -tto (fatto, detto, letto, scritto), -so (preso, perso, chiuso, deciso), -sso (messo), -sto (visto, chiesto, risposto), -erto (aperto, offerto). The full list is on the reference page, and the Verbs page shows every participle.

items.t: Ho fatto il codice fiscale a Lecce. Ho preso il treno delle sette.
items.n: I did the tax code in Lecce. I took the seven o'clock train.

items.t: Antonella ha detto: manca la marca. Ho letto le istruzioni, ho scritto tutto, ho messo la firma.
items.n: Antonella said: the stamp is missing. I read the instructions, wrote everything, put my signature.

items.t: Hai visto Chiara? — No, non l'ho vista oggi.
items.n: Have you seen Chiara? — No, I haven't seen her today.
items.note: l'ho vista: the participle agrees with a preceding la (unit 10)

items.wrong: Ho fatto → ho faciuto; ho dicuto; ho prenduto
items.right: ho fatto; ho detto; ho preso

blocks.title: Ordinals and dates
blocks.rule: Primo to decimo are their own words; from 11 on, drop the final vowel and add -esimo (undicesimo, ventesimo, trentatreesimo). Ordinals are adjectives and agree: la prima volta, il terzo piano, le prime due. Written: 1°, 1ª, or 1º. Dates use cardinals except the first.

blocks.note: Numbers ending in -tré and -sei keep the vowel: ventitreesimo, ventiseiesimo.

items.t: L'ufficio anagrafe è al primo piano, sportello tre.
items.n: The registry office is on the first floor, counter three.

items.t: È la seconda volta. La prima volta mancava la marca.
items.n: It's the second time. The first time the stamp was missing.

items.t: Il primo maggio è festa. Il due giugno è la Festa della Repubblica.
items.n: 1 May is a holiday. 2 June is Republic Day.
items.note: dates: only the first is ordinal

items.t: Papa Francesco, Luigi XIV (quattordicesimo), il XXI (ventunesimo) secolo.
items.n: Pope Francis, Louis XIV, the 21st century.
items.note: kings, popes and centuries take ordinals, often in Roman numerals

items.t: Prendi la prima a destra e la seconda a sinistra.
items.n: Take the first right and the second left.

items.wrong: il tre primo, il uno maggio
items.why: Ordinals have their own forms; dates use cardinals except the first.

items.wrong: la primo volta, il prima piano
items.right: la prima volta, il primo piano
il ventunesimo secolo / il XXI secolo

blocks.title: da: since and for, with the present
blocks.rule: Something that started in the past and is still true takes the present tense + da: abito qui da due mesi (I've lived here for two months), dal primo giugno (since 1 June). Ask with da quanto tempo…?

head: Italian (present + da)
English (present perfect)
rows: Abito a Roccamarina da due mesi.
I've lived in Roccamarina for two months.
Ho la cittadinanza da due anni.
I've had citizenship for two years.
Dora has known Pasquale for fifty years.
Da quanto tempo è a Roccamarina? — Da due mesi.
How long have you been in Roccamarina? — Two months.
Da quando studi l'italiano? — Da settembre.
Since when have you studied Italian? — Since September.

blocks.title: The English trap
blocks.text: English uses the present perfect: *I have lived here for two months*. Italian uses the plain present, because you still live here. [[Ho abitato qui da due mesi]] is wrong; it would mean you no longer do. The passato prossimo + per is for finished periods: [[Ho abitato a Toronto per trent'anni|I lived in Toronto for thirty years]] (and then left).

items.t: Da quanto tempo aspetti? — Da un'ora. Ho il numero dodici da un'ora.
items.n: How long have you been waiting? — For an hour. I've had number twelve for an hour.

items.t: Nando lavora al bar da trent'anni. Ha lavorato a Milano per due anni, prima.
items.n: Nando has worked at the bar for thirty years. He worked in Milan for two years, before.
items.note: present + da (still true) vs passato prossimo + per (finished)

items.wrong: Ho abitato qui da due mesi.

items.why: Da, not per, for a period that continues.

blocks.title: Lei at the counter
blocks.rule: In an office, Lei in both directions. The verb is third person (ha, vuole, può), the pronouns are Le (to you) and La (you), and instructions come as formal imperatives: mi dica, si accomodi, firmi qui, torni giovedì, aspetti un attimo.

head: They say
English
Form
rows: How can I help? Go ahead.
Ha un documento? Ha compilato il modulo?
Do you have ID? Have you filled in the form?
Sign here. Write in block capitals.
Aspetti un attimo. Torni giovedì. Prenda il numero.
Wait a moment. Come back Thursday. Take a number.
Do you need anything else? Can I help you?

blocks.caption: You say
head: Italian
English
rows: Good morning. I'd like to do / request / renew…
Scusi, dov'è l'ufficio…? A che sportello?
Excuse me, where is the … office? Which counter?
Ho un appuntamento alle dieci con la dottoressa Moro.
I have an appointment at ten with Dr Moro.
Che documenti servono? Quanto costa? Quanto tempo ci vuole?
What documents are needed? How much is it? How long does it take?
Può ripetere, per favore? Non ho capito.
Can you repeat, please? I didn't understand.

items.why: Lei forms in an office, both ways.
Titles are used; dottore / dottoressa for any graduate.

sections.title: L'accento che cambia tutto
sections.intro: Italian writes the accent only when the stress falls on the last vowel, and in a handful of words to tell them apart. But every word has a stressed syllable, written or not, and getting it wrong changes the word or makes it unrecognisable. A1 ends with a review of stress.

blocks.caption: Written accents that distinguish words
head: With accent
Without
Both
rows: Dora dà le chiavi da un mese.

head: Pattern
Examples

MOdulo, NUmero, TAvolo, SAbato, TElefono, MEdico, aNAgrafe, SPICcioli, CElibe, NUbile
verbs: io / tu / lui / loro on the stem; noi / voi on the ending
comPIlo, comPIli, comPIla, comPIlano · compiLIAmo, compiLAte
compiLAto, riceVUto, fiNIto · FATto, DETto, PREso (irregular: on the stem)
cittÀ, perCHÉ, venerDÌ, caFFÈ, lunedÌ, giÀ, piÙ

pairs.nb: he / she filled in (passato remoto, unit 17)
pairs.tip: The accent at the end turns the present into a literary past.
Same word; only the second is wrong.

blocks.title: Two habits to keep
blocks.text: Type the accents: the exercises accept a missing one as "almost right", but an Italian form, a name on a document, an email, do not. And say the loro form of every verb with the stress on the stem: [[PARlano]], [[LAvorano]], [[comPIlano]]. It is the one thing in pronunciation that marks a learner more than the r.

items.t: È già giovedì? Sì. Dà la marca, la mette là e firma.
items.n: Is it Thursday already? Yes. She hands over the stamp, puts it there and signs.
items.note: è · già · sì · dà · là: five written accents

items.t: Gli impiegati compilano i moduli e timbrano i documenti.
items.n: The clerks fill in the forms and stamp the documents.
items.note: comPIlano, TIMbrano

sections.title: Tocca a te · A1 checkpoint
sections.intro: Thirty exercises on this unit, then a ten-exercise A1 checkpoint that mixes everything from units 1 to 8. If you get eight or more of the ten, you are ready for A2.

sections.title: Il comune e le carte
sections.intro: The codice fiscale, residency, the stamp from the tobacconist, the photocopies, and the one skill the Italian state teaches better than any school: patience.

blocks.text: Sixteen characters built from your surname, first name, birth date, sex and birthplace: [[FRRLCU96C12Z404X]] is a Luca Ferrante born in Toronto on 12 March 1996. You need it for everything: a rental contract, a phone contract, a bank account, the health card, a job, a gym. It is issued free by the [[Agenzia delle Entrate]] (the tax agency) on the spot, with a passport, or by an Italian consulate abroad before you leave. Get it first; nothing moves without it.

Registering as resident ([[iscrizione anagrafica]]) at the comune makes you officially a citizen of that town: it gives you the health card, the ID card, the right to vote locally if you're a citizen, lower utility rates, and a place in the system. You need an ID, the codice fiscale, proof that you live at the address (a registered rental contract or the owner's declaration), and for non-EU citizens the permesso di soggiorno. Italian citizens by descent, like the protagonist, just need their citizenship recorded. After the application a [[vigile]] visits the address to confirm you really live there; be home, or leave your name on the bell and the mailbox. The certificate arrives within forty-five days, in theory.

blocks.title: The kit
blocks.text: Before any office: the original and two photocopies of every document, front and back; passport photos; a [[marca da bollo]] of sixteen euros (from a tabaccheria, never from the office); cash for fees; a pen; the form already filled in, in block capitals ([[in stampatello]]); and the number from the machine, taken on arrival. If the office opens at 8:30, the queue starts at 8. If they say [[torni giovedì]], go Thursday, not Friday.

Italy grants citizenship by descent ([[iure sanguinis]]): a child of an Italian citizen is Italian, whenever and wherever born, as long as the line was never broken by renunciation. Millions of Italo-Canadians, Italo-Argentines and Italo-Americans qualify through a grandparent or great-grandparent, and consulates have waiting lists of years. The rules were tightened in 2025 to limit how far back the line can go; anyone with an Italian parent or grandparent should check the current rules at a consulate. The protagonist did it in Toronto, with nonno Cosimo's birth certificate from this same comune, and the whole file took two years. Antonella's two visits really are a record.

Much of Italian bureaucracy has moved online and needs a digital identity, [[SPID]], which you get from a provider with your codice fiscale and an ID, and sometimes a certified email address, [[PEC]], which is legally equivalent to registered post. Both are unit 22. For now: the comune still has a counter, a number machine and Antonella, and for residency you go in person.

blocks.title: Pazienza
blocks.text: An Italian office is not slow out of malice. It is slow because every document protects a clerk from a mistake, every stamp proves someone checked, and every rule was written after someone cheated. The people behind the counter are mostly competent and often kind, and they will help the person who arrives prepared, polite and with the Lei. [[Dottoressa]], a [[grazie, molto gentile]], and a smile at the second visit buy more than any argument. [[Fatto]] is worth waiting for.
